whyCheapBearCase.answer: PSKY trades below book value (P/B 0.88) with negative trailing ROE (-4.98%) [source: 1], but this is heavily distorted by one-time items: the company reported a net loss of $586 million for the Successor period August 8-December 31, 2025, driven substantially by transaction and purchase-accounting effects following the August 7, 2025 change-of-control transaction that combined Paramount Global and Skydance under the Ellison family [source: 5, 6]. The much larger, live bear case is the pending, contested acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery: in July 2026, twelve state attorneys general (California, Arizona, Colorado, Connecticut, Massachusetts, Minnesota, Nevada, New Jersey, New Mexico, New York, Oregon and Washington) filed an antitrust action seeking to block the WBD Merger, and on July 24, 2026 Paramount stipulated that the deal will not close, and integration will not begin, until the earlier of five days after the court's ruling or June 1, 2027 [source: 2, 3]. If the merger fails to close for regulatory reasons, Paramount owes WBD a $7.0 billion Regulatory Termination Fee, which would likely require issuing additional, dilutive equity [source: 2]. This deal-risk overhang is corroborated by a same-week cached headline: 'Paramount Skydance (PSKY) Stock Sees Fair Value Cut As Deal Risk Clouds Analyst Views' (2026-08-09) [source: 8]. This is a real, filing-confirmed, binary-outcome bear case tied to litigation risk, not merely a market overreaction.

revenueEpsTrend.answer: Mixed and complicated by the August 2025 purchase-accounting reset, which makes clean year-over-year comparisons difficult. Revenue grew modestly: Q2 2026 $6,913M vs Q2 2025 $6,849M (+0.9%); H1 2026 $14,260M vs H1 2025 $14,041M (+1.6%) [source: 4, 6]. Operating income grew faster - Q2 2026 $475M vs Q2 2025 $399M (+19.0%); H1 2026 $1,091M vs H1 2025 $949M (+15.0%) [source: 4, 6] - but this partly reflects the absence of a $157M content/lease impairment charge that hit both the Q2 and H1 2025 comparison periods [source: 4]. Despite improving operating income, net earnings (Parent and noncontrolling interests) actually declined for H1: $216M in 2026 vs $222M in 2025, down 2.7% [source: 4, 6], because interest expense rose to $493M (H1 2026) from $431M (H1 2025, +14.4%) on merger-related financing, and depreciation and amortization jumped to $726M (H1 2026) from $175M (H1 2025, +315%) - the latter driven by amortization of the $1.5 billion of trade names and $1 billion of affiliate-relationship intangible assets recognized in the August 2025 purchase-accounting basis reset [source: 4, 5]. I am not presenting a diluted-EPS year-over-year percentage change because the transaction created an entirely new share structure (hundreds of millions of new PSKY shares issued, prior Paramount Global shares cash-settled or converted), making the pre- and post-transaction per-share figures not directly comparable [source: 5, 6].

marginTrend.answer: Mixed. Operating margin improved: 6.9% in Q2 2026 ($475M / $6,913M) vs 5.8% in Q2 2025 ($399M / $6,849M), up about 1.0 percentage point [source: 4] - though this is flattered by the absence of the $157M impairment charge recorded in the 2025 comparison period. Net margin, by contrast, appears to have compressed: net earnings of $216M on $14,260M of H1 2026 revenue (1.5%) versus $222M on $14,041M of H1 2025 revenue (1.6%) [source: 4, 6], with the gap explained by sharply higher interest expense and D&A from merger financing and purchase-accounting intangible amortization, as detailed above. I cannot cleanly separate a 'true' underlying operating margin trend from these one-time and financing-related distortions using only the two filings extracted here.

guidanceChange.answer: Not confirmed from available sources, though there is a suggestive signal. A cached headline dated 2026-08-09, 'Paramount Skydance (PSKY) Stock May Be Below Fair Value As Guidance Rises,' implies a possible guidance increase, but only the headline was cached - the article content was not fetched, so I cannot confirm what specific guidance metric rose or by how much [source: 7]. No explicit forward-looking numeric guidance range was located in the extracted MD&A or Risk Factors text of either filing. I am not asserting a guidance change occurred based on the headline alone.

catalysts.text: Operating income grew faster than revenue in both Q2 2026 (+19.0% vs +0.9%) and H1 2026 (+15.0% vs +1.6%), partly reflecting improved cost discipline and the absence of the prior-year impairment charge - a genuine (if partially one-time-item-driven) operating improvement.

The pending Warner Bros. Discovery acquisition, if it clears the antitrust challenge and closes, would create a significantly larger, more scaled media and streaming company - Paramount raised its offer to $31.00 per WBD share, indicating continued strategic commitment to the deal.

A same-week cached headline suggests analysts see the stock as potentially undervalued with rising guidance ('Stock May Be Below Fair Value As Guidance Rises,' 2026-08-09) - a live, dated bullish signal, though based on headline text only.

risks.text: Active, unresolved antitrust litigation: twelve state attorneys general sued in July 2026 to block the WBD Merger, and Paramount has stipulated the deal cannot close until the earlier of five days after a court ruling or June 1, 2027 - a real, binary, court-dependent risk to the company's largest strategic initiative.

A $7.0 billion Regulatory Termination Fee is payable to WBD if the merger fails to close for regulatory reasons, which management states would likely need to be funded via additional equity issuance - a large, real, quantified contingent liability with direct dilution risk for existing shareholders.

Structural, management-acknowledged secular decline in linear television revenue that is 'expected to persist,' with standalone streaming growth potentially 'insufficient to offset' the decline if the WBD Merger does not close - a real business-model risk independent of the litigation.

Rising leverage and interest costs tied to merger financing (a senior secured bridge term loan facility) are already visible in the numbers - H1 2026 interest expense was up 14.4% year-over-year even before the full incremental WBD financing is drawn - plus separate, ongoing shareholder litigation (the Baker, Gabelli, and NYCERS actions in Delaware Chancery Court) relating to the original Skydance/NAI transaction.

verdict.reasoning: The filing evidence shows underlying operating trends that are modestly positive - revenue growing low-single-digits and operating income growing double-digits in both Q2 and H1 2026 [source: 4] - which argues against a simple 'broken business' story. But this is dominated by an enormous, binary, court-dependent risk that neither the quant screen nor a standard fundamentals read can resolve: a live, twelve-state antitrust lawsuit against the company's transformative WBD acquisition, a stipulated closing delay to as late as June 1, 2027, and a real $7.0 billion termination-fee liability if the deal collapses for regulatory reasons [source: 2, 3]. Negative trailing ROE and a null P/E further reflect the still-unsettled purchase-accounting aftermath of the August 2025 Ellison-family transaction rather than a clean read on ongoing profitability [source: 1, 5, 6]. Confidence is low, not medium, because the single largest driver of this stock's near-term outcome is a pending court ruling on the antitrust challenge that cannot be predicted from financial filings, and because the purchase-accounting basis change makes several 'normal' fundamental comparisons (especially EPS) genuinely not comparable year-over-year.
